rows.en: "Flag 1B0 has not been set. To play this private
event, set flag 1B0 and try again.
Otherwise, the event will be forcibly terminated."<FC:B4:3E>
Yamato: "Well, we're back, but what are we going to do?"
Take a break.
Listen to Yamato's explanation again.
Leave the room.
Touya: "I'm tired... I think I'll get some sleep
until we arrive..."
Yamato: "Huh? Are you really sure?"
Touya: "I've had enough. I'm going to sleep."
Yamato: "Oh, Touya... Honestly!"
Touya: "You get some rest too. Without sleep, you won't be
any use when we need you."
Yamato: "All right, all right. I understand.
I think I'll go to sleep too, then... Heave-ho."
Touya: "...You sound like an old lady."
Yamato: "How rude! Here I am, a beautiful unmarried lady,
and you go and say something like that!"
Touya: "...Heh heh heh."
Yamato: "?"
Touya: "...Hey, Yamato..."
Yamato: "What is it?"
Touya: "What's going to happen to us now?"
Yamato: "...Do you want to go home?"
Touya: "Well, even if I went home, it'd just be the same days
over and over again... I don't mind either way, but..."
Yamato: "But?"
Touya: "...No, it's nothing.
Well, good night."
Yamato: "Good night."
Touya: (Kasumi, Koichiro... I wonder how they're doing...)
Yamato: "Again? Sure, I don't mind.
I'll explain as many times as it takes for you to understand."
Listen properly.
Never mind.
Yamato: "...Ahem! Well, the first thing you need to do is
meet someone. Nothing will happen until you do."
Touya: "Huh? Isn't that obvious?"
Yamato: "Then do you know how to find them?
Do you even know who's where?"
Touya: "Of course I don't. I'll just have to try rooms at random."
Yamato: "Heh heh heh! Well, I happen to knyow!
With my purrsonal sensor!
I can tell exactly where everyone is!"
Touya: "...What's this 'purrsonal sensor' of yours?
I get that it's a personal sort of sensor, but..."
Yamato: "Heh! Well, that's... something I don't really understand either."
Touya: "...Hey."
Yamato: "I-I'm joking, honestly! Um, it seems to be a function
that picks up a particular person's brain waves.
So I can instantly tell who's where.
It actually had a much more complicated name,
but it does the same thing, so I came up with my own name.
Well? Pretty nifty, isn't it?"
Touya: "Well, it certainly is handy.
Did Gabon install that too?"
Yamato: "That's right."
Touya: "...Sheesh, that old guy even put something like that in..."
Yamato: "It's useful, so what's the problem? Apparently, it's
actually meant for emergencies. It seems to detect when
someone's brain-wave pattern differs from the registered one."
Touya: "When their pattern's different?"
Yamato: "Hmm... When they're emotional, or in distress,
or thinking very strongly about something..."
Touya: "So, when something unusual is going on?"
Yamato: "Exactly. So if you go and see someone I've detected,
chances are, something will happen.
Well, I suppose it isn't guaranteed."
Touya: "I see. Well, let's get started..."
Yamato: "Stooop! I'm nyot finished yet.
There's one more important thing.
You can just chat normally, but sometimes you'll want to
talk about topics you've picked up through your actions, right?"
Touya: "W-Well, yeah, but..."
Yamato: "Then just press the Y button and
select 'Topic List.' It'll show you all the important
information you've gathered so far. From there,
choose the word you want to discuss, then just speak
to the person you want to ask. That's all you need to do."
Touya: "Huh... But that person won't necessarily know
anything about it, will they?"
Yamato: "Tsk, tsk, tsk! You'll see when you look, but each topic
clearly says who it's for, so don't worry.
Someone's name appears in '( )' after the word,
and the topic you've selected is shown too,
so you're all set."
Touya: "Then I guess that's all right..."
Yamato: "Oh, right! About those topics...
You can't just select as many as you like."
Touya: "...What do you mean?"
Yamato: "There's a number called Topic Points.
When you choose a topic and talk to that person, you lose 1 point.
And once that number reaches 0,
you can't select any more topics.
So you need to think carefully about your choices
instead of just picking everything at random."
Touya: "Sounds like a hassle."
Yamato: "Don't say that.
The world's nyot so forgiving that you can
just wing your way through it."
Touya: "Yeah, yeah."
Yamato: "Hmm, what else do I need to explain...?
Ah, 'Move,' I suppose."
Touya: "What's that?"
Yamato: "It's a point-to-point movement system for when
walking around the map is a hassle. Select it,
and it'll display the names of various places in the Liebhofen.
Choose one of them,
and you can instantly move there. Handy, isn't it?
But you should walk around yourself until you get used to the place.
If you use this too much, you'll lose track of
where you actually are.
Each floor of the Liebhofen has a simple layout,
but there are five levels, so don't let your guard down."
Touya: "Yeah. You're right."
Yamato: "Good, you're listening. And finally,
when you feel you've done enough, select 'Finish.'
That will end this part."
Touya: "Right."
Yamato: "That's a quick explanation, but it covers everything.
Now the best thing is to try it yourself and get a feel for it."
Yeah, I get it. Let's go, then.
Could you explain that again?
Yamato: "Okay. So what are we going to do now?"
Rest until we arrive.
Leave the room.
Touya: "Clovis, you're in there, right? Can I come in?"
Clovis: "Oh, Touya! Hang on, I'll open up!"
Touya: "Yeah."
Clovis: "..."
Touya: "Huh? You're looking kind of pale..."
Yamato: "...?"
Clovis: "Eeek! A m-monster cat!"
Touya: "H-Hey, why'd you shut the door?!
Monster cat...? Oh!"
Yamato: "...Come to think of it, he couldn't stand me.
And that's the second time he's called me that! How mean!"
Clovis: "Touya, I'm sorry, but I'm no good with cats.
I can't let you both into my room. Sorry!"
Yamato: 'I'll wait out here.'
Touya: 'You don't need to go out of your way.'
Yamato: 'But...'
Touya: 'It's fine. We didn't have any important business anyway.'
Yamato: 'Really?'
Touya: "Clovis! We just remembered something we have to do,
so we're going."
Clovis: "I'm really sorry! Come by again...
Oh, when your partner isn't with you."
Touya: "Yeah, see you."
Yamato: "Why does he hate cats so much, I wonder?"
Touya: "Who knows? He'll tell us himself
when he feels like talking about it."
Arthur: "Yes?"
Touya: "It's Touya..."
Arthur: "Oh, please come in."
Yamato: "Wow..."
Arthur: "Is something the matter?"
Touya: "No, I was just thinking how different all the rooms are..."
Arthur: "Really? Aren't they all the same?"
Yamato: "They're the same size, but... what's inside..."
Touya: "Yours really has a personality of its own..."
Arthur: "I see. Should I simply take that
as a compliment?"
Touya: "Yeah. The layout's very Arthur,
and I think it's nice."
Yamato: "Though there's a hint of the occult about it..."
Arthur: "I-Is there...?"
Yamato: "Wow! What's this, I wonder?
There are so many things I've never seen!"
Touya: "Hey, don't go touching things without asking."
Yamato: "I knyow that."
Arthur: "Heh heh... I expect great things from you in the future too."
Touya: "You say that, but..."
Arthur: "What are you saying?
No one has ever learned to pilot a Spirit Mech this quickly
and achieved results in actual combat as you have.
Even we needed a fair amount of training to reach this point,
so have some confidence in yourself."
Touya: "Confidence, huh..."
Arthur: "In any case, we don't know when the enemy will make a move.
They could attack at any moment,
so let us continue fighting together."
Touya: "Sorry, but I still can't give you a definite answer.
Something's still bothering me..."
Arthur: "I see..."
Yamato: "Touya, Touya!
Look at this! I've never seen anything like it!"
Touya: "Hey! I told you not to..."
Arthur: "Ha ha ha, I don't mind.
And if anything's troubling you, please feel free
to talk to me at any time.
After all, we're among the few people from the same homeworld."
Touya: "Yeah. We'd probably never have met
if this hadn't happened. Sorry to bother you."
Arthur: "Huh? Didn't you have some business with me?"
Touya: "It's done. I just wanted to say hello, really."
Arthur: "I see. That's a good thing to do.
Well then, good luck."
Touya: "Yeah. Come on, Yamato, let's go."
Yamato: "Huh? Hey, wait!"
Yamato: "There are so many things in the world that we
don't knyow about! I'm amazed."
Touya: "Of course there are. Even back in Japan, where we live,
there's still plenty we don't know about.
What you see in front of you isn't everything."
Yamato: "That's true too."
Touya: "..."
Yamato: "..."
Ai: "Hmm? Oh, Touya."
Touya: "What... are you doing?"
Ai: "What do you mean? I'm baking cookies, obviously."
Touya: "Cookies...?"
Ai: "Well... I promised her...
That we'd make cookies together next time...
She was... just an ordinary fourteen-year-old girl..."
Ai: "Hmm? What's wrong?"
Touya: "...N-No, nothing... Anyway...
How do you manage to destroy
this much just by baking cookies?"
Ai: "S-Shut up!
This was an unfortunate accident that happened entirely by chance."
Touya: "Looks to me like an inevitable, human-caused outcome,
actually."
Ai: "Argh! Shut up, shut up, shut uuup!
I'm busy, so go away! Shoo, shoo!"
Touya: "That's pretty harsh..."
Help her.
Leave quietly.
Ai: "Huh?"
Touya: "I said I'll help."
Ai: "I-It's fine. I can do it myself..."
Touya: "..."
Ai: "Ah! Hey! Don't just start messing with things!"
Touya: "...It's to cheer that girl up, right?
You said you'd made a promise.
Let me help too."
Ai: "Touya..."
Touya: "Can't I?"
Ai: "Thanks. But I have to make these myself.
<FC:3C:3E><FC:04:3C:16:03>All by myself..."
Touya: "I see..."
Ai: "Sorry."
Touya: "I hope... the cookies turn out well."
Ai: "Yeah."
Touya: "Well then, good luck."
Ai: "Leave it to me."
Touya: "...Yeah, yeah. I get it.
You want me to go somewhere else, right? See you."
Ai: "Oh, Touya. What's up?"
Touya: "Nothing. How are the cookies coming along?"
Ai: "As if there could be any problems!
They're so perfect, it's scary."
Touya: "R-Right..."
Ai: "Well, there you have it. No need to worry."
Touya: "Okay. See you, then."
Yamato: "She'll get sick of you if you keep pestering her.
Let's leave her alone."
Touya: "...You think so?"
Yamato: "I knyow so! Come on, let's go!"
